description: The old name check() implied a non-mutating predicate (consistent with Rust naming conventions: is_*, has_*, contains_*). The function actually calls HashMap::remove() — it fires once and is consumed. A caller reading check() would reasonably assume repeated calls are safe; they are not. take_fault signals: (a) ownership transfer via 'take' (idiomatic Rust: Option::take, Cell::take, HashMap::remove), (b) fault injection context via 'fault'. A contributor might suggest consume_fault or pop_fault, but 'take' is the strongest conventional signal in Rust for 'remove and return'. Renaming back to check() or any check-prefixed form would re-introduce the misleading read-only implication.
title: take_fault name accurately signals remove-and-consume semantics (not a read-only check)
